subject: Budget range validation: monthly spend band & procurement thresholds
messages:
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -0700
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Iyer <rajiv@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acmepay.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Subject: Post-call recap & budget range validation - Acme Payments

Rajiv / Sophie — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can finalize a model and get procurement moving on your side.

Summary of what I heard:
- Workload: real-time transaction enrichment + fraud scoring on 3M transactions/month. Typical prompt: ~120 tokens input + ~60 tokens output on average (we measured ~180 tokens/interaction).
- Peak concurrency needs: low (burst to 150 qps), average steady-state around 20 qps.
- Quality target: parity with your current provider for fraud scoring (we'll run eval set).

Pricing datapoints I promised to validate: unit economics and likely monthly spend bands given the token volumes. Pls confirm if my understanding of volumes is correct; I did quick math below and flagged where I made assumptions.

Assumptions / calculations (please confirm):
- 3,000,000 transactions/month * 180 tokens/txn = 540,000,000 tokens/month (~0.54B).
- Redwood hosted list price (example): $1,200 per 1M tokens for this model tier (we'll provide shaded discounts for committed volume).
- At $1,200 / 1M tokens -> baseline monthly cost = $1,200 * 540 = $648,000/month.
- Typical enterprise committed discount bands move this closer to $400-900 / 1M depending on commitment & term.

Budget bands (rough):
- Conservative (40% discount): ~$388k / month
- Mid (60% discount): ~$259k / month
- Aggressive (70%+ discount & dedicated routing): ~$194k / month

Ask for you: 1) confirm the 3M txn/month and average token per txn (180) are accurate; 2) if you have a target $/1M tokens or target monthly spend band (e.g., <$100k, $100-250k, $250-500k, >$500k) that procurement will sign up for; 3) procurement thresholds (PO minimums, procurement cycle time, any need for an SOW or custom SLAs).

Next steps I suggest:
- If volumes look right, I can produce a 12-month TCO with breakouts (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private) and a recommended committed band for discounts.
- If procurement needs a PO threshold or different contracting flow to accept an annual commitment, pls share the Acme procurement contact and any template.

Attaching the 1M-token breakdown I promised and a template procurement spreadsheet — filling those out will let us give a firm committed price.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up with Dev (SE) if you want a technical walkthrough of batching/kv-cache options that can materially reduce token usage.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachments: Redwood-pricing-1M_tokens-breakdown.pdf

Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
From: Rajiv Iyer <rajiv@acmepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acmepay.com>
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & budget range validation - Acme Payments

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications:

- Volumes: 3M txns/month is right for Q3 baseline. There is upside in Q4 but we should price for Q3 baseline.
- Tokens: the 180 tokens/txn number seems reasonable — our current provider's logs show ~150-200 depending on metadata size.
- Procurement: target monthly budget band is $200k–$400k. We have procurement rules that require a formal RFx + PO for >$250k annual spend; for contracts >$250k/month we need executive approval (CFO).

Procurement contact: Sophie is the buyer on our side (cc'd). She can share the vendor form and PO thresholds.

Next: please send the 12-month TCO and a clear committed discount recommendation (what threshold gets us to ~$200k/month vs $400k/month). Also flag any assumptions on average tokens and batching that would lower cost.

Appreciate it — Rajiv

Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 13:04:00 -0700
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Iyer <rajiv@acmepayments.com>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acmepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Subject: RE: Post-call recap & budget range validation - Acme Payments

Rajiv / Sophie — quick note from engineering on levers to reduce token spend that Marissa mentioned:

- Prompt templating: removing repetitive metadata from prompts and moving it to server-side context reduces input tokens per txn by ~10-20% in our experience.
- KV cache/prefix caching: for repeated entities (merchant metadata) we can cache embeddings/kv tokens and avoid re-sending large metadata on every call — could drop tokens by ~15-30% depending on hit rate.
- Batching & compression: for non-real-time enrichment we suggest batching 5-10 txns where acceptable (saves overhead tokens).

If we assume conservative 20% token reduction from templating + 15% from caching (sequential gains), the effective tokens/txn could move from 180 -> ~122. That would place monthly tokens at ~366M and reduce costs proportionally.

Happy to run a quick proof-of-concept on a sampled day of logs if you share an anonymized sample. That output will let us give a tighter $/1M estimate and a recommended committed band.

— Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marissa / Dev — thanks for the fast follow-up. Confirming next steps from Acme procurement side:

- We can proceed with a POC and a 30-day eval (expected spend during POC ~ $10k-15k). Procurement will only engage legal/PO for contracts that exceed $50k total commitment.
- For production, finance prefers monthly invoices via PO. Thresholds: PO template for > $50k, executive approval required for > $250k/month as Rajiv noted.
- Our target for procurement sign-off without executive escalation is to keep initial committed band <= $250k/month. If Redwood can show credible reduction levers (as Dev outlined) and a price point of ~$200k/month with a predictable model, we can move forward without CFO.

I'll attach the vendor form and PO thresholds — filling that will speed legal/procurement.

Sophie
Procurement Manager | Acme Payments
